title: Typed rawArgs render channel + fix the xdev __partialJson two-valued key
wave: M4 Wave C — Hợp đồng render (shippable: false — merges with M4-4/M4-6 into one M4 changelog decision; §6.2 forbids shipping any M4 wave alone)
one_line: Give renderers a properly typed `rawArgs: { json, complete }` channel on the options object, actually forward the whole options object to extension renderers (today two adapters silently drop four fields), and stop `__partialJson` from meaning two different things at once.
user_visible_effect: A `xd://` device card and any extension-registered tool card stop showing a frozen or wrong raw stream mid-stream: a renderer that watches the raw argument buffer repaints on every prefix growth instead of only when the parsed args object identity changes, and an out-of-repo extension can finally observe `argsComplete` / `executionStarted` (and the new `rawArgs`) on its `renderResult` — fields that have been declared in the TUI type since forever but were thrown away at the two adapter sites before the extension ever saw them. The `__partialJson` key no longer shows up in the JSON tree headed for the model under the wrong name.

test_contract:
Three observable contracts, one of them the deciding row.

(1) EXTERNAL STREAM MONOTONICITY (packages/tui/test/tool-execution-xdev-render.test.ts). Stream a `write` whose path is `xd://probe` in increasing argument prefixes through a real `ToolExecutionComponent`; the mounted `probeTool.renderCall` records the `options.rawArgs.json` it is handed. Contract: the recorded strings are monotonically non-decreasing in length, each is a prefix of the next, and the last one is the OUTER write-call buffer (it contains `"path":"xd://probe"`), NOT the inner device payload (which contains `"command"`). Consumer-observable failure: a `xd://` device card whose raw preview freezes at the first parsed checkpoint, or — the bug this item exists to prevent — shows the inner device JSON while the outer stream is still growing, so the card misrepresents how much of the call has arrived.

(2) REBUILD/LIVE PARITY (same file). Drive the same tool call twice — once through the live reveal path, once through the ui-helpers.ts:605 rebuild path — and assert both produce byte-identical final render. Consumer-observable failure: a card changes appearance when the user changes theme, toggles a setting, or refocuses mid-stream. This defends the third path the plan mislocated; note the plan's stated file (chat-transcript-builder.ts) is the wrong file entirely and would leave this contract undefended.

(3) THE ADAPTER REACH CONTRACT (packages/coding-agent/test/extensions/raw-args-render-channel.test.ts) — the deciding row. A tool registered through `registerTool({ renderResult })`, wrapped by `RegisteredToolAdapter` (and separately by `customToolToDefinition`), receives `rawArgs`, `argsComplete` and `executionStarted` on its options. Consumer-observable failure: an out-of-repo extension that gates its streaming preview on `options.argsComplete` renders as though nothing ever completed, forever, because the field is declared in the type and thrown away at the adapter. This test is green on a fix that only adds the field to the interface, and green on the built-in `xd://` path alone — that is precisely what makes it the deciding row, and it is the one thing `bun run check:ts` provably cannot catch.

Negative assertion required in (3): an option field that was never present must not appear, so the adapter fix cannot regress into an untyped blanket passthrough that would also leak internal render bookkeeping to extensions.

Not a contract, do not test: that the interface has N members; that `rawArgs` exists; that the code 'ran'.

gate:
Four gates. Each is mechanical and each can go red.

G1 — ADAPTER REACH (the deciding gate). `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/extensions/raw-args-render-channel.test.ts` goes RED on the pre-change tree and GREEN after. It goes red because `RegisteredToolAdapter.renderResult` receives `options.argsComplete === true` and asserts the captured object still has it, and today wrapper.ts:62 has dropped it. To confirm the gate is real, do this: add ONLY the `rawArgs` field to the two interfaces and change nothing else, re-run, and observe it stay GREEN — that is the proof the gate has teeth beyond a type edit, and it is the exact trap the plan names.

G2 — STREAM MONOTONICITY. In packages/tui/test/tool-execution-xdev-render.test.ts, the recorded `rawArgs.json` sequence is asserted non-decreasing and prefix-chained, and the final value asserted to contain `"path":"xd://probe"` (outer) and NOT be the inner device JSON. Goes red if the channel is populated from the inner decode or is never repainted mid-stream.

G3 — REBUILD PARITY. Same file: the rebuild-driven render equals the live-driven render. Goes red if ui-helpers.ts:605 is not wired — a failure mode that is invisible to both `bun check` and the built-in-only xdev tests.

G4 — HIDDEN-KEY NEGATIVE. `HIDDEN_ARG_KEYS` (json-tree.ts:23) covers the new xdev key. Assert via `formatArgsInline` — the same seam packages/tui/test/json-tree-render.test.ts:32 already uses — that neither the old nor the new spelling appears in the rendered output. Goes red the moment someone renames xdev.ts:57 and forgets this line, which is the plan's stated silent risk.

G5 — TYPES. `bun run check:ts` exits 0.

All five are able to fail on incomplete work. G1 is the one that distinguishes this item from a type-only change.

risk:
The single most likely way to get this wrong is shipping a type-only change that is green everywhere and reaches nothing. Adding `rawArgs` to `RenderResultOptions` and `ToolRenderResultOptions`, and stopping there, produces: a green `bun run check:ts` (both interfaces are structurally satisfiable), a green built-in `xd://` test (the TUI passes `this.#renderState` wholesale, so built-ins see any new field for free), and zero change for any extension — because `wrapper.ts:62` and `sdk.ts:1217` rebuild the options object from three named fields and discard everything else. The field would be declared and unreachable, and the two already-declared fields `argsComplete` and `executionStarted` would remain invisible to extensions exactly as they are today. Nothing in the type checker can see this, and the built-in test cannot either. G1 exists solely to catch it; write G1 first, before touching the production code, and watch it go red.

The runner-up is getting the step order wrong: fixing the adapter forwarding before the `updateArgs` short-circuit would let a raw-consuming renderer miss repaints during the intermediate state, and renaming the magic key before the typed channel exists would leave every built-in reader (bash.ts:196-237, edit.ts:251, eval.ts:98) reading a key nobody writes. Both failures are silent — they produce a plausible-looking card, not an error.
open_questions: WHICH KEY gets renamed? The plan says only 'Cuối cùng mới bỏ khoá ma thuật' (finally remove the magic key) and its risk note says a rename 'without updating the hidden list makes the key show up in the JSON tree'. It never says WHICH key. The two candidates are genuinely different jobs. RECOMMENDED: rename only the INNER key written at xdev.ts:57 (a 2-site change: xdev.ts:57 and the strip at xdev.ts:114, plus json-tree.ts:23) and make `rawArgs` purely ADDITIVE for the outer stream. That preserves bash.ts / edit.ts / eval.ts untouched and leaves the six literal-pinning test files valid as written. The alternative — retiring `__partialJson` entirely from the outer args object and moving bash/edit/eval onto `options.rawArgs.json` — is the reading that matches the plan's expectation that all six test files need updating, and it is roughly 3x the surface. DECISION PROCEDURE: this is a maintainer call, not an implementer call, because the two branches ship different amounts of renderer churn under one changelog decision. If nobody decides, take the recommended branch and record the deviation in the PR description.

Should `rawArgs.complete` be redundant with the existing `argsComplete`? `RenderResultOptions` already carries `argsComplete?: boolean`, and `rawArgs.complete` would say nearly the same thing. Two sources of truth for one fact is a drift risk. RECOMMENDED: keep both for now — `argsComplete` is set from `setArgsComplete` (a lifecycle event) while `rawArgs.complete` describes the buffer the renderer actually holds — but if the implementer finds the two can disagree, that disagreement IS the finding and should be raised, not smoothed over.

Does the M4 changelog decision (§6.2) get a user-facing line about `argsComplete`/`executionStarted` now reaching extensions, separate from the `__partialJson` rename line? The plan treats the adapter fix as 'cùng một dòng, và nó đóng một bug đang sống' (same line, it closes a live bug) — i.e. not separately user-visible. Confirm that reading before the PR is written, because the changelog is a single decision for all of M4 and an out-of-repo extension author is exactly who would notice.

Is `renderContext` supposed to be fixed in this PR too? The same two adapters drop it (`#renderState.renderContext` is set at tool-execution.ts:959 and :1121, and `RenderResultContextOptions` at renderer.ts:30 exists precisely to carry it). The plan mentions only `argsComplete` and `executionStarted`. RECOMMENDED: do NOT fix it here — it is a separate observable behaviour change and this item is already at three waves' worth of churn. But record it as a known follow-up, because leaving it means the adapter forwarding fix is still partial and the next reader will not know that was a decision.

plan_corrections.claim: Plan §M4-7 'Chi tiết' bước 1: 'sửa short-circuit ở `tool-execution.ts:388-394`. Early return ở `:392` nằm trên `#displayInputVersion++` ở `:394`, nên một renderer tiêu thụ raw sẽ không repaint giữa stream' — phrased as a live defect being fixed.
plan_corrections.verdict: MISFRAMED — the line numbers are right, the diagnosis is not
plan_corrections.correction: The short-circuit is correct TODAY. `displayArgsForPrefix` allocates a fresh args object on every frame where the raw prefix grew (`const rawPrefixChanged = entry.exposeRawPartialJson && prefix !== entry.displayPrefix;` at :424, then a new literal at :428), returns `changed: true`, and `#tick` only calls `updateArgs` inside `if (display.changed)` (:614-616) — so args reference identity changes exactly when the raw prefix grew, and `#displayInputVersion++` does fire. The early return at :392 is sound. It becomes UNSOUND only as a consequence of step 2: once `rawArgs` is a side channel, the decoded args can be reference-identical while `rawArgs.json` grew, and the guard would swallow the frame. So step 1 is not a bug fix, it is the guard-rail that makes step 2 safe — which is why the ordering is load-bearing. The plan's own text ('nhưng phải tiến version khi chỉ phần tiền tố raw đổi') states the right requirement; only the framing as a pre-existing defect is wrong, and the comment at :388-391 ('Callers always allocate a new arg object on each streamed delta') becomes false at exactly the moment step 2 lands and must be rewritten, not preserved.
plan_corrections.evidence: tool-args-reveal.ts:424 `const rawPrefixChanged = entry.exposeRawPartialJson && prefix !== entry.displayPrefix;`; :427-429 fresh literal + `changed: true`; :613-616 `const display = displayArgsForPrefix(...); if (display.changed) { entry.component.updateArgs(display.args, id); ... }`. tool-execution.ts:392 `if (args === this.#args) return;` sits above :394 `this.#displayInputVersion++;`, and :800 confirms the version feeds the repaint key.
